name: Uruvo
author: uruvo

sections.description:
Uruvo creates translated drafts as WordPress posts and pages. Review each draft
in WordPress before publishing. The built-in language tools can also link
translations you add by hand and provide localized URLs and a language switcher.

The translation editor supports published posts, pages and eligible public
custom post types using Gutenberg core blocks or the Classic Editor.
Enable other types of content in Uruvo > Languages > More content to translate.
Review custom fields and taxonomy terms separately. Uruvo’s hosted translation service offers a shared
word allowance across connected sites or unlimited translated words on one registered site.

Use the WordPress demo to review a sample
Spanish translation and save an editable draft without creating an account.

External Services

Automatic hosted translations use Uruvo, an external
service that requires an account with a translation allowance. A site
administrator explicitly connects the site using its account URL and key.
Once connected, requests to Uruvo authenticate that site, submit selected
public content and language settings, retrieve translation results, and
check the account’s word balance. Source edits are queued automatically
only when the administrator enables that option. Uruvo uses Cloudflare Workers
AI to process the selected text. Published translations are stored in the
site’s WordPress database.

Adding a site language can request a language pack from WordPress.org. Site
language setup and manual translation linking are available locally without
connecting a Uruvo account.

Uruvo Terms of Service ·
Uruvo Privacy Policy ·
Cloudflare Privacy Policy

In standalone mode, the site administrator selects and runs the translation
worker and authorizes access with a site-specific key.

Source and credits

Uruvo bundles a modified build of Polylang under GPL-3.0-or-later.
THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt contains the copyright notices, changes and build
information. Source for the bundled language assets
sections.installation:
1. Activate Uruvo.
  2. In Uruvo > Languages, choose the language your site already uses and click Add language. Add a language to translate into.
  3. Add your WordPress site in the Uruvo dashboard.
  4. Open Uruvo > Settings from the WordPress sidebar and paste the connection key.
  5. Open Translate, select content, and estimate the target languages before queueing.
  6. Filter Translate by status to find work that needs an update or is ready to review. Review the changes and publish the selected translations together when safe. To bypass review for a new translation, opt in to automatic publishing before queueing.
sections.faq:
Can I edit translations before publishing?

Yes. Open the translation job to create an editable WordPress draft.

Does Uruvo support page builders?

Uruvo supports common text fields in Elementor and Beaver Builder, and
the classic SiteOrigin Page Builder layout. Start with one staging page.
Uruvo flags widgets that need manual review before automatic publishing.

How do I get help?

Use the Uruvo support form.
sections.changelog:
0.9.4

  • Add the Uruvo Language Switcher block and shortcode with locale flags, native language names, keyboard navigation and search for long language lists.
  • Keep the selected language in WooCommerce block and classic checkout.

0.9.1

  • Keep language setup notices within the relevant WordPress screens.
  • Improve translation strings, validation, and escaping.
  • Fix activation with PHP 8.1.
  • Prefix new jobs and settings with Uruvo while keeping existing translations and worker connections compatible.

0.9.0

  • Filter content by target language and translation status, then review and publish changes to live translations in a batch.
  • Keep existing edits during review and show the next action on stuck jobs.
  • Check a published page as a visitor and prepare a personal migration preview from WordPress.
  • Add an opt-in pilot for translated classic WooCommerce cart, checkout, account pages, and customer order emails.

0.8.0

  • Translate supported Elementor, Beaver Builder and classic SiteOrigin layouts into editable drafts.
  • Keep builder styles and media references, localize links to published translations, and flag unsupported components for review.

0.7.2

  • Support Single-site Unlimited connections and show translation usage without a word balance on that plan.

0.7.1

  • Show the WordPress content-language filter only on lists it can filter. Use the language filter inside Uruvo for translation content.
  • Find content with no language assigned directly from Languages.
  • Show connection setup in place of queueing on disconnected sites.
  • Show job review and refresh actions where they apply.

0.7.0

  • Add site languages from a searchable dropdown with readable regional names.
  • Set the original language of existing content and enable public content types from Uruvo.
  • Request WordPress language packs in the background where available.

0.6.0

  • Add opt-in automatic publishing and bulk draft approval or publication.
  • Skip linked translations by default and direct users to work already in Jobs.
  • Move language management under Uruvo and localize core admin workflows in Spanish, French and Hindi.

0.5.0

  • Add a WordPress sidebar entry, guided setup, source-language filters and translation coverage.
  • Keep batch selections across content filters and show an estimate against the available word balance.
  • Open a single translation job immediately and show live status, side-by-side copy review, and publishing links.

0.4.0

  • Add separate Translate, Jobs and Settings screens with batch selection and live job status.
  • Translate enabled public custom post types into drafts of the same type.

0.3.3

  • Browse and search published pages and posts from the Uruvo screen.

0.3.2

  • Show when hosted translation is waiting for daily capacity.

0.3.1

  • Clarify hosted translation setup, data processing, and source credits.

0.3.0

  • Connect to Uruvo’s hosted translation service or an administrator-managed worker.
  • Review translations as native WordPress drafts before publishing.
